I have almost got all the parts for my NON AR-15. What's a NON AR-15 you may ask. Well the AR-15 is a 5.56 mm NATO rifle, but the NON-AR15 is of different calibers. What I am building up is a NON AR-15 in 6.8 Remington SPC. Why a 6.8mm SPC you may ask. Well the 6.8mm SPC is primarily a hunting cartridge because it has a lot more terminal energy over 250 meters than the 5.56. In Fact the 6.8 mm SPC has about 80% of the energy of a 7.62X51 (.308 Winchester). This will be an excellent gun for Hogs (if you live in Texas) antilope, Mule and White Tail deer out to over 600 meters. Also the 6.8mm SPC can be loaded with projectiles from 85 grain all the way up to 120 grain projos. The 6.8mm SPC is just slightly less accurate than the 6.5mm Grendel. In case you guys are mathematically challenged 6.8mm is .277 or the same caliber as the .270 Winchester in a much smaller cartridge case Any way back to the rifle. I am using a AR-Precision CMV Nitrided 20 inch Match barrel. I am also using the Syrac Gas piston as this is an adjustable gas piston. This allows you to tune the rifle to the particular cartridge you are using. This tuning controls the speed of the bolt carrier as it moves to the rear. This is why it is reported that gas piston rifles shoot a lot softer than direct gas impinging rifles. The using of a piston moves the heat of the rifle up to the barrel and not into the chamber area. Hot gas is very bad on lubricants and ammunition. Hot powder has different burning characteristics than cold powder. The gas piston system makes the rifle a lot easier to clean as there is no carbon build up in the upper receiver or in the bolt carrier that you have to scrape out. Once I get it built up I will post a picture of it here. Keep tuned.

Im trying to find a mechanical keyboard that has the escape and caps lock switched. Do you fine folks know of any vendors? Or is this a custom job that id have to attempt?

If you can't find a board with switched caps, there is a work around. With Windows OS you could use SharpKeys to re-bind the keys you want, with Linux there is software built in (I presume to all versions) that you can use to re-map the keys in question (You may want to further google this as I haven't used Linux in years).

You could custom order keys with your own text from WASD Keyboards here that will fit any standard Cherry MX mechanical keyboard. Chose R4 1x1 for the little Esc key, and R2 1x1.75 for the longer CapsLock key as seen here. You could instead order a keyboard with blank keycaps if you can touch type well.

Smaller board may suit you well like the Pok3r, Ducky Mini or KBT Pure Pro. If you want full size; Das Keyboard, Filco, Ducky, CoolerMaster, Leopold and WASD CODE are all brilliant brands.

Hope this helps :)
